The 30-year, by a wide margin. Its lower payments pay down principal more slowly, so interest accrues on a larger balance for twice as long.

At 6.5%, per $100,000 borrowed, the 30-year costs about $127,500 in interest versus about $56,800 for the 15-year. Lenders usually price 15-year loans at a lower rate too, which widens the gap further.

The cost of the 15-year is a payment roughly 38% higher ($871 vs $632 per $100k at that rate), which matters if the money would otherwise earn more than the mortgage rate.
